intervals.label: civil construction of underground laboratory
intervals.note: Closes a gap the original pass explicitly left uncovered ('no source... states an explicit approval date between the 2015 CDR and the 2021 start of detector installation'); the JUNO Collaboration's own performance paper gives this date directly. End date is the day the detector's Stainless Steel support-structure installation began, per the same source.
intervals.quote: The civil construction of the JUNO underground lab started in January 2015.

intervals.label: detector support-structure, acrylic-vessel and PMT installation
intervals.note: Replaces the earlier single 'installation' interval (2021-2024-12, confidence approximate, sourced only to a search-engine summary of an IHEP report) with day-precision dates verified directly in the JUNO Collaboration's own paper.
intervals.quote: The installation of the Stainless Steel support structure started on 19 December 2021. The installation of the photomultiplier tube (PMT) modules and electronics boxes started on 23 October 2022 and finished on 17 December 2024.

intervals.label: filling with ultrapure water and liquid scintillator
intervals.quote: During the first two months, the inner and outer spaces of the acrylic sphere will be filled with ultrapure water. Over the following six months, the ultrapure water inside the acrylic sphere will be replaced with liquid scintillator.

intervals.label: physics data taking
intervals.quote: JUNO began physics data taking on August 26, 2025

placements.note: Superseded the earlier 'start 2021, approximate' value (drawn from a search-engine summary) with the day-precision date verified directly in the JUNO Collaboration's own Initial performance results paper (arXiv:2511.14590 = Chin. Phys. C 50, 043001 (2026)).
placements.quote: The installation of the Stainless Steel support structure started on 19 December 2021

energy_resolution.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: prior quote ('anticipated energy resolution of "3.02%/√E (MeV)"') was not verbatim -- the abstract says 'effective energy resolution', not 'anticipated'. This is the pre-operation design target. The first measured performance (Chin. Phys. C 50, 043001 (2026)) reports 3.4% at 0.511 MeV -- see result:juno-initial-performance-2026.
energy_resolution.quote: we expect a yield of 1345 p.e. per MeV and an effective energy resolution of 3.02%/\sqrt{E (MeV)}$ in simulations

pmt_count.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: the prior value (20000) was the 2015 design target/2024 IHEP press-release rounding, not the as-built count. The JUNO Collaboration's own Initial performance results paper (arXiv:2511.14590 = Chin. Phys. C 50, 043001 (2026)) gives the actual installed count: 17596 20-inch PMTs (4939 Hamamatsu R12860-50 dynode-PMTs + 12657 NNVT GDB6201 MCP-PMTs). A separate array of 25587 3-inch PMTs (per the same source; IHEP's press release rounds this to 25,000, the 2021 design paper projected 25,600) forms a complementary double-calorimeter system; recorded in `subsystems` rather than as a second `pmt_count` (not an Appendix A key for a second array).
pmt_count.quote: The main system consists of 17596 20-inch PMTs, (referred in the following as 'large PMTs') installed on the SS structure. Two types of PMTs have been employed: 4939 dynode-PMTs ... and 12657 Micro-Channel Plate photomultipliers, MCP-PMTs

target_mass.quote: The central detector contains 20,000 tons liquid scintillator with an acrylic sphere of 35 m in diameter.

description.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: the as-built count (25587) replaces the earlier IHEP press-release rounding (25,000).
description.quote: In addition, 25587 3-inch PMTs (referred in the following as 'small PMTs') have been produced from Hainan Zhanchuang Photonics Technology (China) and installed in the space between the 20-inch PMTs.
description.value: A complementary array of 25,587 3-inch photomultiplier tubes providing an independent, non-saturating energy measurement alongside the 20-inch PMT array

description.quote: The veto system is used for muon detection, muon induced background study and reduction. It consists of a Water Cherenkov detector and a Top Tracker system.
description.value: A water-Cherenkov detector plus an overhead Top Tracker system used for muon detection and cosmogenic-background rejection

subsystems.name: Water Cherenkov veto and Top Tracker

summary.plain: A 20,000-tonne sphere of clear liquid, watched by more than 17,000 large light sensors and over 25,000 smaller ones, sitting inside a pool of water that screens out stray particles.
summary.technical: 20 kt liquid-scintillator central detector in a 35 m acrylic sphere, read out by 17,596 20-inch PMTs (4,939 dynode + 12,657 MCP) and 25,587 3-inch PMTs, immersed in a water-Cherenkov veto pool with an overhead Top Tracker; design energy resolution 3.02%/√E (MeV), first measured at 3.4% for 0.511 MeV γ-rays.

technology.quote: The central detector contains 20,000 tons liquid scintillator with an acrylic sphere of 35 m in diameter. ... The veto system ... consists of a Water Cherenkov detector and a Top Tracker system.
technology.value: 20-kiloton liquid-scintillator sphere viewed by large- and small-diameter photomultiplier tubes, immersed in a water-Cherenkov veto pool with an overhead Top Tracker
